name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a 4-pixel focus ring with a 2-pixel offset around every interactive element. This ensures keyboard users can see where they are without blocking content, meeting WCAG 2.2’s 2:1 contrast for focus indicators. The trade-off is slightly more visual noise, but it’s necessary for clarity and compliance.

name: Reader
text: The 4-pixel focus ring still poses a risk of blending into busy backgrounds, and the 2:1 contrast ratio may not be enough to ensure visibility. A better alternative would be to use a high-contrast focus ring with a 3:1 or 4.5:1 contrast ratio, which would provide clearer visibility without overwhelming the content. This decision could be settled by testing the focus ring with various background patterns and images to determine the minimum contrast ratio required for clear visibility.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt a 3:1 contrast focus ring—solid 2-pixel width, 2-pixel offset—on every interactive element. This meets WCAG 2.2’s minimum for focus visibility without the visual clutter of a 4-pixel ring, balancing clarity and subtlety. The trade-off is slightly less prominence than a 4.5:1 ring, but it keeps the interface clean while still ensuring keyboard users can track focus reliably.

name: Reader
text: A 3:1 contrast focus ring still risks blending into patterned or image-heavy backgrounds, especially on mobile where screen glare reduces perceived contrast. Test it on a high-contrast image background with a keyboard-only user—if the ring disappears or becomes hard to spot, we must use a 4.5:1 ring or a thicker 3-pixel ring with a 3-pixel offset.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship **3px outset focus ring, 4.5:1 contrast, 2px spacing**—verify touch/mobile visibility and keyboard nav. Owner: Ramp.
